CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH RAI K  ORAL ORDER

This petition is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarika Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short,
'BNSS') for grant of anticipatory bail in Crime No.60/2024 dated 15.06.2024 registered by Shahabad Town Police for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 417 and 420 of IPC.

2. The factual matrix of the case is that, the complainant, namely, one Rohit Vijaykanth Patil,
resident of Bhankur village, Shahabad Taluk was running a tea business near Bhankur cross from 4 years and the petitioner and his family members are running cloth business in the name and style of "Standard Cloth Center"
and they also running a chit fund in the name and style NC: 2026:KHC-K:6 HC-KAR "Batiya Chit Fund", Finance in the name of "Batiya Finance and Investment Corporation", and also a "Sahayog Money Saving Scheme" in Shahabad from 40 years.

3. Things stood thus, the complainant started to deposit Rs.1,000/- on daily basis in the Saving Scheme introduced by the petitioner and other accused persons and the same was entered in a passbook from 01.08.2020 till March 2024.
The complainant, in total, deposited a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- in the Saving Scheme, subsequently the petitioner and other accused persons failed to return the said amount.

Thus, the petitioner and others cheated the complainant to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/- and on enquiry it was also revealed that the petitioner along with accused persons cheated other 74 persons who were invested in the said Savings Scheme.
Hence, he lodged a complaint against the petitioner along with other accused persons.

sentences.text: Based on the complaint, the respondent-police registered a case against the petitioner and others in NC: 2026:KHC-K:6 HC-KAR Crime No.60/2024 as stated supra by arraying petitioner as accused No.2.
Ever since the registration of FIR, the respondent-police are making hectic attempt to arrest the petitioner.

As such, on the apprehension of arrest, the petitioner approached the IV Addl. Dist. &
Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi, Sitting at Sedam, for grant of anticipatory bail in Cri.Misc.No.842/2025 along with accused Nos.3 and 4.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Sessions Judge by partly allowing the said petition, granted anticipatory bail to accused Nos.3 and 4 and rejected the bail petition of the petitioner i.e. accused No.2.
Hence, this petition.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent- State.
6.
Apart from urging several contentions, learned counsel for the petitioner primarily contended that the petitioner is the son of accused No.1.
At the time of the alleged incident, the petitioner was aged about 20 years NC: 2026:KHC-K:6 HC-KAR and he was pursuing his B.Com. Degree.

Further,
he has not at all involved in the alleged transaction in any manner, since the entire cloth shop and other business were run by his father.
Accordingly, prays to allow the petition.

7. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader opposes the bail petition on the ground that the investigation is still under progress and the custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required for recovery of the alleged amount.
Hence, he prays to dismiss the petition.
8. I have given my anxious consideration both on the submission made by the learned counsel for the respective parties so also perused the materials available on record.

9. As could be gathered from records, the complaint lodged by the complainant reveals that from the year 2020 to 2024, he has invested a sum of NC: 2026:KHC-K:6 HC-KAR Rs.5,00,000/- in the Savings Scheme introduced by accused No.1, who was a cloth merchant also running a chit fund business and introduced the Savings Scheme.
10. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner, this petitioner-accused No.2 is the son of accused No.1.

The Trial Court has granted anticipatory bail to accused Nos.3 and 4, who are none other than the younger brother and mother of this petitioner on the ground that there was no involvement of them in the alleged transaction.
In such circumstances, this petitioner is also entitled for anticipatory bail on the ground of parity.
Hence, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, suffice to hold that the petitioner is entitled for anticipatory bail.
11. The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest registered in Crime No.60/2024 by Shahabad Town Police Station,
Kalaburagi, for offences NC: 2026:KHC-K:6 HC-KAR punishable under Sections 406, 417, 420 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1) The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Angad Sindh Bhatia vs The State Of Karnataka on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51920601/
